title: Deliberation-integrity guards: duration floor, discussion evidence, timestamp sanity
description: D-001 went from case-open to publish in 71 seconds, with four identical priors, four final ballots identical to the priors, and stamps three days in the FUTURE of the wall clock. None of that is illegal today. Three guards: (1) a deliberation cannot conclude without at least one recorded discussion round per alternative; (2) final ballots identical to priors across ALL voters is flagged on the record as NO-DELIBERATION-OBSERVED (flag, not block: unanimity can be honest); (3) timestamps in the future of the machine clock refuse the write. Each guard carries its negative control.

notes.note: Plan: (1) new discuss verb (eligibility-gated, non-empty text, existing alternative, status deliberating) + conclude refuses unless every alternative carries at least one discussion round with non-empty text, re-validated at conclude so hand-edited empties do not count; (2) all-ballots-identical-to-priors flagged NO-DELIBERATION-OBSERVED on the record, flag not block; (3) any recorded stamp in the dossier beyond machine clock + 300s skew refuses every WRITE verb (generic recursive stamp scan, exhaustive over the dossier), reads stay open. Drive-by: T-417 verifier non-blocking finding 2 (non-dict colegiado value crashes) converted to clean fail-closed refusal. NOTE on the title's duration floor: NOT implemented as a wall-clock threshold; no such threshold is ratified (currency.py doctrine) and the discussion-evidence guard is the mechanical replacement -- 71 fast seconds with real recorded discussion per alternative is legal, zero discussion is not, however slow.

HANDOFF -> verifier: T-418 built: three deliberation-integrity guards, each answering a D-001 defect, each with its negative control. (1) DISCUSSION EVIDENCE: new 'discuss' verb (eligibility-gated, non-empty --text, --re must name a real alternative, status must be deliberating); conclude REFUSES unless every alternative carries at least one non-empty round, RE-VALIDATED at conclude so a hand-edited empty round or one pointed at a nonexistent alternative counts for nothing. Deliberate design note: the task title says 'duration floor' but I did NOT implement a wall-clock threshold -- no such threshold is ratified (currency.py doctrine) and speed is not the defect, absence of discussion is; 71 fast seconds WITH real discussion is legal, zero discussion is not however slow. (2) UNANIMITY FLAG: every final ballot identical to its voter's own prior -> record carries deliberation_flag=NO-DELIBERATION-OBSERVED; flag NOT block (unanimity can be honest); does not fire if any voter arrived without a prior or any ballot differs. (3) FUTURE-STAMP REFUSAL: exhaustive recursive scan of every ISO-shaped leaf in the dossier; any stamp beyond machine clock + 300s skew refuses every WRITE verb (sponsor/prior/discuss/vote/conclude); reads (show) stay open so a tampered dossier is auditable; unparseable stamp fails closed; skew constant is engineering tolerance not a constitutional threshold. Drive-by: T-417 verifier round-2 non-blocking finding 2 (non-dict colegiado value crashed with AttributeError) converted to clean 'roster inconsistent' refusal. Evidence: pytest .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py -q -> 41 passed (was 24); full suite 815 passed, 4 skipped. Regression class TheD001DefectCannotRecur replays D-001's shape under the live roster + guards together: clerk proposer never opens the dossier, and a legitimate non-clerk docket still cannot conclude without discussion. Files: .harness/bin/deliberate.py, .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py. Verify hints: try to conclude with a discussion round whose text is whitespace; try a future stamp nested in a ballot; check the flag fires on the exact D-001 priors==ballots pattern; check reads survive a future-dated dossier.

VERIFIED (adversarial replay, scratch roots only, live .harness/deliberations + roster.json untouched -- confirmed via git diff --stat clean). Replay: pytest .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py -q -> 41 passed; full suite -> 815 passed, 4 skipped (matches hand-off exactly). Guard 1 (discussion evidence): whitespace/tab-only --text refused at write; empty --re refused; --re pointing at nonexistent alt refused; hand-edited discussion rounds with empty text, blank text, and orphaned re='' all still refused at conclude (re-validation confirmed, not just write-time check); conclude succeeds once every alternative genuinely discussed. Guard 2 (unanimity flag): exact D-001 shape (4 voters, 4 identical priors==4 identical ballots) fires NO-DELIBERATION-OBSERVED and conclude still succeeds (flag not block, tally present); does NOT fire when one of 4 voters has no prior, or when one ballot differs from its prior. Guard 3 (future-stamp refusal): skew boundary exact -- 299s and exactly 300s ahead allowed, 301s ahead refused (matches documented > skew, not >=); stamp buried 4 levels deep in a new key inside list-of-lists-of-dicts caught; future-dated dossier stays readable via show (exit 0) while sponsor/vote/conclude on the same dossier refuse; unparseable stamp fails closed (covered by suite, replayed). Drive-by fix: non-dict colegiado value (list) now refuses cleanly with 'roster inconsistent ... is not an object' instead of crashing -- confirmed exit 1, no traceback. NON-BLOCKING FINDING: the future-stamp scan walks only leaf VALUES, not dict KEYS -- a future ISO stamp placed as a JSON dict key (e.g. hand-edited {future_ts: "note"}) is not caught (schedule succeeded, exit 0, no refusal). This does not defeat the guard's actual purpose: no live write verb ever emits a timestamp as a key (created_at/recorded_at/voted_at/at/concluded_at are always values), so this is unreachable through the CLI and does not let a forged D-001-style dossier's real audit stamps evade detection -- filed as a doctrinal caveat on the 'exhaustive over every leaf' docstring claim, not a rejection ground. Duration-floor substitution judged SOUND not a dodge: T-418's acceptance_criteria array is empty, the operative spec is the task description which itself defines guard 1 as discussion-evidence (not a wall-clock number), no threshold is ratified elsewhere (consistent with currency.py doctrine of refusing unratified thresholds), and TheD001DefectCannotRecur regression class replays D-001's actual shape under the live roster + guards together and shows it can no longer conclude -- the substitution closes the real defect end to end.

Post-verdict hardening (verifier's non-blocking finding folded in): _stamp_leaves now scans dict KEYS as well as values, so a future ISO string smuggled as a key -- {future_iso: note} -- is caught too, making the 'exhaustive over every leaf' claim true. One regression test added; deliberate.py suite 42 passed. Behavior only tightened; T-419's adversarial replay verifies the hardened version.

SENT BACK by T-419 adversarial replay (harness-verifier / verifier-t419). Guard 1 (discussion
evidence) has a real, blocking escape: undiscussed_alternatives() re-checks discussion rounds
against dossier["alternatives"] at conclude time, but if "alternatives" is hand-edited to []
or the key is deleted after voting, the missing-alternatives list comprehension is vacuously
empty and conclude SUCCEEDS with a full Condorcet tally despite ZERO discuss calls ever having
been made on the dossier. Guards 2 and 3 are unaffected (independently re-verified separately
and still hold). Full reproduction with two independent repros (empty-list and key-deletion
variants), plus 4 additional attack vectors that held (rename-after-discussion, timestamp
boundary in a new nesting shape, unicode-lookalike clerk name, non-dict colegiado with
retrofitted clerk charter), are recorded on T-419's own note (this same timestamp window).
Fix needed: undiscussed_alternatives()/cmd_conclude must not treat an empty or absent
"alternatives" field as "nothing left to discuss" -- either check against alternatives
captured immutably at propose time, or refuse conclude outright when alternatives is
empty/missing on a dossier carrying final_ballots. Needs a dedicated regression test (existing
suite has none: grep -n "alternatives" test_deliberate.py shows every test only ever sets
alternatives at propose time or hand-edits "discussion" entries, never "alternatives" itself).

HANDOFF -> verifier: Round 2: T-419's blocking escape closed in the mechanism. The escape was that emptying the dossier's 'alternatives' field (or deleting the key) after voting made undiscussed_alternatives() vacuously [] so conclude passed a zero-discussion docket. Fix: new effective_alternatives() derives the required-discussion set from the UNION of declared alternatives + every candidate named in a ballot + every candidate named in a prior. The candidates are written into the ballots the tally runs on, so emptying 'alternatives' removes nothing that must be discussed. undiscussed_alternatives() and conclude both key on the effective set. Defense in depth: conclude refuses 'no alternatives to decide among' when the effective set is empty (alternatives emptied AND no ballot/prior names a candidate) -- a conclusion on nothing is malformed. discuss now accepts any effective alternative so a write-in candidate that will need discussion can always be discussed (no deadlock), while an unrelated string is still refused. Honest path preserved: emptying 'alternatives' but genuinely discussing every ballot candidate still concludes (test). Evidence: pytest .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py -q -> 46 passed (was 42); full suite 824 passed, 4 skipped. 4 new tests replay T-419's exact repro (empty-list and key-deletion variants), the malformed-empty case, and the honest-path non-regression. Files: .harness/bin/deliberate.py (effective_alternatives, undiscussed_alternatives, cmd_conclude, cmd_discuss), .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py. Verify hints: try candidates only in priors (not ballots); try a ballot naming a candidate never declared and never discussed (should refuse); confirm the honest full lifecycle still concludes.
